newsitem.title: ITALY: Face of Albanian anarchy arrested in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Face of Albanian anarchy arrested in Italy.

text.p: An Albanian gunman whose photograph appeared in newspapers around the world was arrested in Italy on Thursday on suspicion of running an illegal immigration racket, police said.

The man, named as Despoti Clirim, 27, was photographed by news photographers in the Albanian port of Durres earlier this week pointing a Kalashnikov assault rifle at crowds of frightened people desperate to board ships leaving the country.
Police in the southeast port of Brindisi said Clirim had been arrested on Thursday morning on board a coach carrying refugees from Albania to a reception centre.
His arrest followed publication by a local newspaper of his photograph in Durres and a second taken in Brindisi.

Police said Clirim, who was found in possession of 900 German marks ($530), had told officers he travelled to Italy on a boat that ran into trouble earlier this week off the southeast coast. The 290 people on board were rescued by coastguards.
Clirim was being investigated for links with Albanian and Italian crime groups and would be held in detention, police said.
More than 10,000 Albanian refugees have poured into Italy in the past week in a flotilla of ramshackle craft.

Italian officials say they have evidence that refugees have been charged large sums for berths on the decrepit boats by racketeers in Durres who are exploiting the unrest to run an illegal emigration scam.
Italy says it will grant genuine refugees temporary asylum but will forcibly repatriate Albanians considered a threat to public order.
Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said around 100 "undesirables" had been flown from Italy to Tirana airport on Thursday following the repatriation of some 300 on Wednesday.
